objections.description: AC-CLOSE4 hard-codes a sha256 hash (5da1fd78cc3dd34ce629a75b2021ecab8dea870908efbc559b887f1eee48a5b2) as a required QA gate for /root/.claude/hooks/posttool-subagent-track.py. A whole-file SHA gate can FALSE-FAIL on any unrelated change to the file (e.g., a comment edit, a new helper added by another cycle) even when the WID5 semantic property (helper at lines 114-125 + line 278 calling _record_subagent_call_legacy(bm_path, str(ip_index))) is preserved. Codex adversarial consult independently flagged this same risk and noted that backup-tree SHA already differs (e5b90db3...) from BA's expected hash, while the semantic WID5 property still holds. The semantic check (helper definition + bare str(ip_index) call site) is the correct acceptance criterion; the SHA is over-specified.
objections.suggested_fix: Either (a) downgrade AC-CLOSE4 SHA to advisory/informational rather than required, OR (b) replace SHA equality with a semantic check: 'line 278 contains literal _record_subagent_call_legacy(bm_path, str(ip_index)) AND helper at lines 114-125 returns the in_progress idx via enumerate'. The semantic check is what /redev5 iter1 actually fixed; SHA is incidental.

objections.description: Saga spec internally contradicts itself: §5.3 line 458 designates AC12 as 'known on-site-unreachable goal' AND 'not a precondition for closing engineering work', but lines 590-604 (Step P4) still say AC12 is 'THE central acceptance criterion' and lines 661-662 (Trap 8) still say 'Cycle 3's PRIMARY deliverable is AC12 ... If AC12 is not passed, the user's 彻底彻底修复 requirement is not met'. BA's E4 acknowledges this contradiction but resolves it only at the policy layer (§5.3 line 458 supersedes for closure purposes). A /close Round 1 voter who reads lines 590/661 first could legitimately dissent on Bullet 3 grounds. BA's NS-5 explicitly forbids editing the saga spec, so this contradiction is preserved by design — but the cycle's CLOSE outcome partially depends on /close interpreting §5.3 as the controlling clause for closure. This is structurally weak. Recommendation is documented in BA E4 itself: a future cleanup cycle MAY harmonize sections 5/6/7/8.
objections.suggested_fix: Two options, both acceptable: (a) Accept the structural risk as-is (BA's current path; cycle proceeds); /close evaluators must be primed by the completion-attestation file to read §5.3 line 458 as the controlling clause. (b) If user authorizes a single line edit to the saga spec (NS-5 carve-out), prepend a one-line cross-reference at line 589 or 660 like 'Note: superseded for closure purposes by §5.3 line 458 (AC12 retirement)'. NOT proposing this as a blocking change; recording for visibility.
